newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via three-day system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve was expected to inject reserves into the banking system on Monday via three-day system repurchase agreements (RPs), economists said.

Marc Wanshel, economist at Morgan Guaranty Trust Co, said the Fed's open market desk clearly perceived a substantially larger add need in the current two-week maintenance period than the firm had projected -- roughly $6 billion to $7 billion per day. The Fed added an average of $7.5 billion a day during the first week of the maintenance period, he said.

"We suspected the desk was front-loading reserves in order to avert potential volatility in the funds rate stemming from an expected very low level of banks' average reserve balances at the Fed this settlement period," Wanshel said.
When required balances are low, banks may be forced into interest-rate insensitive sales or purchases of funds to avoid overdrafts on the one hand or idle excess reserves on the other.

However, Wanshel said, thus far in the second week of the period, the Fed has supplied more reserves than Morgan Guaranty thought were needed ($7.8 billion per day), even though funds had been trading below target level. Moreover, the size of the reserve injections have been ratcheting upward over the past three business days, suggesting that some factor was draining more than the Fed initially expected.
Wanshel said a $2.55 billion nine-day fixed term RP arranged last Tuesday remained in effect, but $5.25 billion weekend systems run off.
"We would guess the Fed will replace the latter operation with a comparable-sized three-day RP, perhaps fixed in term," he said.
Fed funds were trading at 5-5/16 percent, slightly above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
(( -- John P. Hughes, N.A. Treasury desk 212-859-1663))
